extracted.intended_audience: women entering or in marriage (wives, mothers, daughters‑in‑law, step‑mothers)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for women about conduct and judgment in marriage and relations‑in‑law, including how to behave toward a husband, mother‑in‑law, other relations, and step‑children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak the truth in love / avoid disagreeable frankness
rubrics_metrics.description: Speak the truth in 'love' — not in temper; do not be needlessly blunt or disagreeably frank when another's comfort is the price thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train yourself to see and call out the excellent qualities in others; frown down rough speech; do not make the Evil One's work easy by being the cause of offences. Anti-patterns: gratuitous, harsh comments that wound and lodge in the mind (compared to a chigoe). Example anecdote: a needless unkind remark comparing a cottage to a charcoal-burner's hut left lasting pain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate appreciation and generous praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Be lavishly generous with pleasant, agreeable expressions (French 'sauce agreable') rather than flattery; give more than the 'grease spot' of criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer praising and accentuating good traits; small courtesies and thankfulness (e.g., thanking a policeman) produce marked positive effects. Anti-pattern: demanding correction of trivial points (the farmer demanding the waiter 'wipe that grease spot off that plate, and bring him some butter').

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not marry to reform a man (marriage is not a reformatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marriage will not, by itself, remake a man's fundamental character; one should not undertake to 'make over' a man who has long indulged wicked passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hopeful fiancee who imagines she can transform a man misunderstands human nature; transient promises during courtship often revert after marriage. Example: a wife who believed she could cure her husband's intemperance died of a broken heart when his habit continued. Anti-pattern: marrying a man expecting marriage alone to cure entrenched vices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess a man's core character before marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's redeemability depends on whether his nature is essentially sound or 'stunted, warped and foul by sin'; long‑established habits are unlikely to be relinquished by marriage alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether defects are temporary or fundamental; do not ignore severe vices simply because some redeeming qualities exist. Anecdote and rhetorical questions used to illustrate consequences for wife and children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love, patience, and tact are essential for marital happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Abundant love, well‑blended with divine patience and woman's especial gift—tact—are necessary for peaceful married life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualities are needed from the start and throughout the marriage to live together peaceably for even the first year. Practical expectation management: understand that lover and husband may show affection differently (e.g., husband wanting dinner and his newspaper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize difference between lover's and husband's expressions of affection
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that the way a man shows affection as a lover may differ after marriage; do not expect continuous courtship behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lover may loiter and speak tender words; the husband may prioritize domestic routine and leisure (e.g., newspaper). Expect practical, less romantic demonstrations of care post‑marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the welfare of future children when choosing a husband
rubrics_metrics.description: A woman must seriously consider whether she is doing irreparable wrong to unborn children by giving them an unprincipled father.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think beyond immediate feelings; consider heredity/influence and the probability that children's lives may be harmed by a father's vices. Declares it reckless and soulless to marry with this clearly in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not romanticize a 'dash of wickedness'
rubrics_metrics.description: The belief that a little wickedness makes a man more interesting is misguided; vice does not ennoble character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotal criticism: the author rails against preferring 'the naughty man' and compares it to throwing pearls before swine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and appreciate your husband's mother
rubrics_metrics.description: A wife should seek to be kind and appreciative toward her mother‑in‑law; the mother who raised the husband deserves recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the mother trained or contributed to the husband's good qualities, give her credit. Avoid sneering at mothers‑in‑law; appreciation enhances marital harmony and gratitude from husband.

rubrics_metrics.name: Husbands should appreciate their wife's mother
rubrics_metrics.description: A husband who loves his wife will show regard for her mother; such affection evidences true love and promotes the wife's happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal respect between husband and wife's mother fosters domestic peace; husbands who acknowledge the mother’s role make their wives happier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not criticise your mother‑in‑law to your husband
rubrics_metrics.description: Never criticise your husband's mother to him; doing so forces him into a disloyal position or causes you to judge him unfeeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If he sympathizes with you he appears disloyal; if he does not you call him unfeeling. Instead, keep criticisms private (or better, withheld) to avoid undermining his filial affection. Example counsel: 'Make the effort to see John's mother with his eyes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use role‑reversal empathy to manage dislike of in‑laws
rubrics_metrics.description: If you dislike an in‑law, imagine your own mother or daughter in that person's place and act accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mental exercise reveals charitable motives and softens judgment; assume the other 'means well' and has not yet learned your ways. Practical remedy for prejudice seeded by societal jokes and ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid preconception and cultural jokes that poison relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Societal lampoon, caricature, and jokes about mothers‑in‑law predispose young people to antagonism and make future harmony harder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize how repeated ridicule becomes self‑fulfilling; refrain from perpetuating pasquinade that puts prospective daughters‑in‑law on the defensive before they meet their mothers‑in‑law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tact and diplomacy in managing relations‑in‑law
rubrics_metrics.description: Management of relations‑in‑law requires conscious tact—do not broadcast every small grievance and avoid actions that force your spouse to take sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid telling your husband every complaint about your family; similarly, avoid complaining about his family to him. Keep family disputes out of his immediate loyalties; be 'not in' when his family quarrels. Example: a wife who never mentioned his family's faults preserved his family's admiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not involve your husband in petty family grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recounting your family's slights to your husband often creates ongoing resentment and causes him to take a defensive, active role that escalates the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small domestic complaints are quickly forgotten by the wife but may be magnified in the husband's mind if he is told; restraint prevents turning momentary annoyances into lasting enmity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step‑mother must deliberately make herself love the children
rubrics_metrics.description: A step‑mother should 'make' herself love her husband's children as a first step toward successful guardianship and affection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the 'hyphen' disadvantage of being a 'step' parent and add patience, tact, and pity. Practical rule: govern children with love rather than nervous harshness; children sense nervousness. Anecdote: horse‑reins metaphor—firm, steady, gentle governance succeeds; nervousness provokes misbehavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step‑mother: avoid harshness; guard the tongue
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not show exasperation or scold sharply; keep a rigid guard upon the harsh tongue because children remember injustices for years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppress quick curt commands ('Stop that noise!') and unjust punishments; children are tender, remember undeserved blows, and will judge actions long afterward. Patience, consistency, and impartiality are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits of an outsider replacing a biological mother
rubrics_metrics.description: No woman, however tender, can truly take an own mother's place; step‑motherhood is different in origin though it can be lovingly and conscientiously performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pretend equivalence; instead, conscientiously fulfil the foster‑mother role and accept that affection may develop gradually. Encourage husband support to overcome children's prejudice.
